name: injured-run
intent: Looped injured/limping locomotion with an asymmetrical rhythm and a guarded upper-body posture rather than a neutral, symmetrical run cycle.

phases.label: rise from the low stance at the start of the loop
open the stride and shift the pelvis toward +X
reverse the transfer direction and descend
recover from the lowest compression and return toward the loop-start pose

keyPoses.role: strongest pelvis shift toward +X / open stride
loop closure / near return to the opening pose

weightTransfer: The pelvis rises from f0 to f5, shifts laterally toward +X and reaches its maximum around f10, descends to its lowest point around f15, then returns near its initial lateral position and height by f19. Support-foot identity and the injured side are not asserted.
bodyMechanics: The pelvis establishes the primary rhythm through rise → lateral shift → drop/compression → return. Chest and shoulder rotation change through the cycle, while the arms counterbalance the torso, producing an asymmetrical and guarded running silhouette.

recommended: asymmetrical run cadence with pelvis rise, lateral shift, and drop/compression
guarded upper-body mechanics and arm counterbalance in injured locomotion
